record.category: udp port forward (demo relay, open-source client)

free_tier.stated: You can give it a try with wstunnel demo server

egress.terms: no allowance published for the demo relay; it is described as a way to check that you can bypass a proxy, not as a service; ingress: udp

record.interface_detail: Documented demo example: wstunnel client -L 'tcp://4443:10.43.0.11:443' -P demo --tls-sni-override=google.fr wss://ws.erebe.dev. Reverse UDP form (client usage, not shown with the demo): -R 'udp://1212:1.1.1.1:53'.
record.chaining: wstunnel -R udp://51820 on any free VM, or the demo relay if it permits the binding; this is the shape that composes with a free compute lane

limits.value: the demo server allowlists one tunnel: 'The tunnel is the only one that is going to be allowed.'

record.binding_note: The demo relay's allowlist is the first thing that fails, before any byte count: the documented example is a single fixed TCP forward, so a reverse UDP binding is not established to be permitted at all.

identity_cost.detail: the demo takes a shared password: '-P demo' with wss://ws.erebe.dev, no account

record.reliability_note: a shared demo endpoint with no stated capacity; the operator can withdraw it without notice
record.confidence_note: Unverified because the demo's UDP permission was not tested and its capacity is unpublished.

evidence.proved: the demo server, the -P demo shared password, the allowlist sentence, and the -R udp:// reverse UDP form in the client usage block

record.notes: The wstunnel client is genuinely capable of a reverse UDP port and is the standard tool for carrying WireGuard over TCP 443. The free part is the demo relay, which is explicitly a courtesy. A self-run wstunnel server removes the courtesy limit but needs a VM of the user's own, so it is the last resort.

extras.wg_detail: the client carries raw UDP both ways and reverse mode binds a port on the server: 'udp://1212:1.1.1.1:53 => listen on server for incoming udp on port 1212 and forward to cloudflare dns 1.1.1.1 on port 53 from local machine'. Whether the shared demo relay at wss://ws.erebe.dev permits a reverse UDP binding is not documented.
extras.volume_stated: no allowance published for the demo relay; it is described as a way to check that you can bypass a proxy, not as a service
extras.transit_note: the wstunnel server unwraps the websocket and emits the datagrams

card.summary: no service and no account; the software is a static binary released under an open licence

free_tier.stated: no service and no account; the software is a static binary released under an open licence

egress.terms: not applicable; the software states no volume, and the tunnel's ceiling is whatever the host and the network in between allow; ingress: tcp

record.tooling: static binary per platform; a systemd unit is the documented server form
record.chaining: a websocket upgrade passes through any TCP or HTTP forwarder that does not buffer, so a free HTTP-only hosted tunnel plus a wstunnel server converts a TCP-only path into a WireGuard path; the wstunnel server still has to run somewhere controlled locally.
record.binding_note: Requires an external server host running wstunnel with a public IP address.

identity_cost.detail: No account required. The client connects to an independently operated wstunnel server.

record.reliability_note: the udp tunnel auto-closes after 30 s idle unless timeout_sec=0; the client sends websocket pings every 30 s by default; MTU must drop to about 1300 or packets fragment
record.confidence_note: measured throughput on a named path would raise it; the README carries only a benchmark image with no numbers in text

evidence.proved: the WireGuard recipe, the udp:// forward with timeout_sec, and the server --restrict-to flag

record.notes: Tunneling software forwarding TCP and UDP over WebSocket or HTTP/2. Designed to traverse firewalls and reverse proxies; WebSocket mode supports traversal through CDNs.

extras.wg_detail: the README ships a WireGuard recipe: server 'wstunnel server --restrict-to localhost:51820 wss://[::]:443' and client "wstunnel client -L 'udp://51820:localhost:51820?timeout_sec=0' wss://my.server.com:443", with the WireGuard peer Endpoint changed to localhost:51820
extras.volume_stated: not applicable; the software states no volume, and the tunnel's ceiling is whatever the host and the network in between allow
extras.transit_note: the bytes cross the wstunnel server, then any CDN or forwarder in front of it
extras.hosting_requirement: a host with a public address running wstunnel server; a user half runs on the device
